source.title: RAD: On-line Anomaly Detection for Highly Unreliable Data
source.authors: Zilong Zhao; R. Birke; Rui Han; B. Robu; Sara Bouchenak; S. Ben Mokhtar; L. Chen

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; figure values are not available as readable text.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests the effect of randomly corrupted labels on classification accuracy, a different measure from training error or memorization.
record.gate_note: Section II reports noisy-label accuracy results for MLP and ResNet classifiers. The cited Zhang et al. result is prior work and is not recorded as this study's result. Figure 1's precise values are not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: Section II tests V4's test-performance component in new datasets using MLP and ResNet under varying random label corruption. It does not measure whether the corrupted training labels are fitted perfectly.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the motivating experiments but omits the paper's main conclusion: RAD and its extensions improve online classification accuracy by filtering suspicious labels and, in some variants, querying an oracle. The authors also report generally worsening test accuracy with stronger label noise, greater MLP robustness than KNN/nearest centroid, and better FaceScrub performance from ResNet than MLP.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates classification accuracy under symmetric random label corruption; it does not use the original random-label memorization experiment or measure training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and classifier differ in their response to label noise; the FaceScrub effect is described as approximately linear, and ResNet performs better than MLP there.

fits_no_version.finding: KNN and nearest-centroid test accuracy deteriorate under label noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random label corruption reduces generalization accuracy in these non-neural classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: RAD filtering and oracle-assisted label correction improve clean-test accuracy relative to learning directly from noisy streams.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Filtering or correcting noisy training labels can improve online classification accuracy.

record.problems: Figure 1 contains the reported accuracy curves, but the supplied text does not expose their numerical values. The study reports test accuracy, not training error, so it cannot establish fitting of the corrupted training labels.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the reported results concern test accuracy under label noise, but do not measure the training-fit behavior required by V4. Figure 1's plotted values are not recoverable from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to near-zero training error with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Relative training time and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption levels, the fully random endpoint at chance, and simultaneous memorization of noise and learning of remaining signal.
Effects of explicit regularization and its removal.
Whether real patterns are learned before noisy labels.

missing.what: Qualitative clean-test accuracy results for MLP on IoT and cluster data and MLP/ResNet on FaceScrub, including IoT MLP's similar accuracy at 50% corruption. The record explicitly omitted these results, but they capture the tested component of V4; exact figure values are unavailable.

record.verdict_notes: Test accuracy directly bears on one component of V4; absent training-error measurements leave the memorization component untested. Later IoT and cluster No-Sel results use KNN and cannot establish the deep-network claim. This study is not an original source for the supplied versions.

versions.untested_parts: Whether these networks fit completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error, with test error at chance, without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Training-set error or perfect fitting; whether test error reaches chance; whether networks capture remaining signal while memorizing noise. The text describes test accuracy degradation but does not provide recoverable figure values.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal.
Whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

relationships.condition: Offline FaceScrub classification with MLP and ResNet
relationships.reason: Text-based verdict; no extracted rows. Section II-B describes approximately linear deterioration of clean-test accuracy as label noise increases, supporting the test-degradation component.
relationships.display_finding: Clean test accuracy deteriorated approximately linearly as label noise increased for MLP and ResNet.
